newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Latin Patriarch sends peace message on Christmas.
newsitem.headline: Latin Patriarch sends peace message on Christmas.

text.p: The Roman Catholic leader of the Holy Land urged the Israeli government in a Christmas message on Friday to start treating Palestinians with dignity.

"The Israeli authorities should change their vision of peace, should take into consideration that the Palestinian human being is equal in his rights and dignity to the Israeli human being," said Michel Sabbah, the Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem.
In his annual holiday message, Sabbah said Israel's closure of the West Bank and Gaza had turned Palestinian towns into prisons and disrupted freedom of worship in Israeli-occupied East Jerusalem.
He said Palestinians and Israelis were living through "some of the most difficult days".

"In this holy land, at this difficult situation in which we are living, we need a saviour in order to put an end to the conflict in which the two peoples are living, Palestinians and Israelis -- a saviour who will bring peace to this land," Sabbah said.
"Our message for Christmas remains peace to all, to Israelis, to Palestinians, to all Arab countries and to all religions and leaders Christians, Moslems and Jews."
Israeli-PLO peace efforts have been dimmed since right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ousted the more moderate Shimon Peres from office in May elections.

Israel's opening of a tourist tunnel near Moslem holy places in Arab East Jerusalem in September sparked heavy clashes between Palestinians and Israelis in which 60 Palestinians and 15 Israelis were killed.

Palestinian areas have been hard hit economically by a closure imposed after Moslem suicide bombings killed 59 people in Israel last February and March. Thousands of Palestinian workers are barred from their jobs in the Jewish state.
Sabbah also expressed sympathy with Israeli Jews whom he said were suffering from a lack of security.
He urged Israel to free some 5,000 Palestinian prisoners, saying their detention harmed peace efforts.
Christians make up a small minority in the Holy Land compared to Jews and Moslems. Christian researchers estimate nearly 200,000 Arab Christians live in Israel, the West Bank and Gaza.
